attempts.summary: Created a sandboxed systemd service `inventory-worker` on node1 that runs a long-running loop writing heartbeat records to /var/lib/inventory/inventory.log. The unit runs as a dedicated unprivileged `inventory` user with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=full, ProtectHome=yes, ReadOnlyDirectories=/, and ReadWriteDirectories=/var/lib/inventory — confining all writes to that one path (systemd 219 on RHEL7 lacks ProtectSystem=strict, so root-read-only + an explicit read-write carve-out was used instead). Confinement was proven from inside the unit's own mount namespace: writes to /etc, /var/lib (outside inventory), and /root all fail with "Read-only file system", while /var/lib/inventory remains writable. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured a healthy pre-restart baseline (boot id, active/enabled service, growing log), triggered `shutdown -r now` whose ack returned before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, and confirmed the boot id changed (809708f3... → 30f6a7b6...) with fresh uptime. Post-restart, the service auto-started (enabled, active), the log file persisted and continued appending, NoNewPrivs=1 held, and the confinement re-check (write to /etc fails, write to /var/lib/inventory succeeds) passed again.
